testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does rough acceleration do?

options.text: It is recommended.
It can damage the engine and transmission.
It is required on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can damage the engine and transmission.
questions.explanation: Always speed up slowly and smoothly. Quick, rough acceleration can damage your vehicle's engine and transmission.

questions.question: When driving, what is important?

options.text: Plan how to handle dangerous situations before they happen.
Enjoy the scenery.
Turn your head all the way around instead of using mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to handle dangerous situations before they happen.
questions.explanation: Watch the road for hazards. Think ahead about what you will do if something dangerous happens.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Only when changing lanes.
Often and regularly.
Only if you think there is a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often and regularly.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. This helps you see traffic around you and spot problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: Which mirrors should you use while driving?

options.text: Do not use the passenger side mirror.
Do not use the driver's side mirror.
Use mirrors on both sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use mirrors on both sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors on both sides while driving. You need to know what is happening behind and beside your vehicle.

questions.question: How should you do a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Follow the same steps in the same order every time.
Do it as quickly as possible.
Ignore small mechanical problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the same steps in the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Use the same inspection method every time. This helps you remember all the important checks and prevents you from forgetting anything.

questions.question: What can cause poisonous fumes to enter a truck's cab?

options.text: A broken exhaust system.
Using the wrong type of fuel.
Not enough oil in the engine.
Tires that are not fully inflated.

questions.correctAnswerText: A broken exhaust system.
questions.explanation: A damaged exhaust system is very dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper area.

questions.question: When going down a long hill, how should you brake?

options.text: Use only the brakes.
Use brakes mostly and downshift occasionally.
Downshift first, then use the brakes.
Never use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift first, then use the brakes.
questions.explanation: On a hill, use your engine to slow down by downshifting. Use the brakes only for extra slowing or stopping if needed.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: No, they are unsafe.
Yes, only on the rear tires.
Yes, only when carrying a heavy load.
Yes, in combination vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they are unsafe.
questions.explanation: Check your wheels before driving for any damage. Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe and should not be used.

questions.question: At an intersection with two left turn lanes, which lane should you use?

options.text: The right lane.
Either lane is fine.
The left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane.
questions.explanation: You may need to swing right to make a safe left turn. Always use the rightmost left turn lane when two are available.

questions.question: What is true about dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They usually have low centers of gravity.
They usually have high centers of gravity.
They are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and need careful handling. The load can also shift while you drive, which affects stability.

questions.question: When driving, rough acceleration is:

options.text: Okay at slow speeds.
Okay at any speed.
Not acceptable at any speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not acceptable at any speed.
questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually. Do not jerk the vehicle. Rough acceleration can damage your engine and parts.

questions.question: The faster you drive:

options.text: The shorter it takes to stop.
The longer it takes to stop.
The easier it is to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer it takes to stop.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds require longer distances to stop. Brake sooner when driving fast.

questions.question: When stopping, press the brake pedal by:

options.text: Pushing down slowly.
Pushing down hard and fast.
Pulling up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pushing down slowly.
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly. This helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: You need an air brake endorsement:

options.text: To operate a vehicle with air brakes.
To drive any truck with a trailer.
To transport hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: To operate a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes test to get a license for vehicles with air brakes or air over hydraulic brakes.

questions.question: Before a trip, make sure that:

options.text: The brake pedal sticks.
The gas pedal is loose.
The pedal grooves have not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal grooves have not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing blocks the pedals. Make sure pedals work properly. Grooved pedal surfaces should not be worn smooth, so your foot does not slip.

questions.question: A vehicle must have all of the following, except:

options.text: A fire extinguisher.
Spare electrical fuses.
Warning devices for a parked vehicle.
A flashlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashlight.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have spare fuses, warning triangles or flares, and a fire extinguisher. A flashlight is not required.

questions.question: If your brakes fail going downhill, decide what to do quickly because:

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle goes.
The longer you wait, the more vehicles get out of your way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle goes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle goes.
questions.explanation: Act quickly when brakes fail on a downhill slope. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle becomes and the harder it is to stop.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from the push rod.

options.text: Two inches
Five inches
One inch

questions.correctAnswerText: One inch
questions.explanation: Before a trip, pull each slack adjuster to check it. It should not move more than one inch from the push rod. If it moves more, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: If driving a truck that requires a CDL:

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only when driving a tank trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: For safety, always wear your seat belt while operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, do all of the following, except:

options.text: Remove your foot from the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Countersteer after the vehicle straightens out.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, release the brake pedal so the wheels can roll again. Steer quickly in the direction you want to go. Then countersteer to prevent skidding the other way.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: Usually thick.
Usually thin.
Not dangerous when driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually thin.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks like a wet road. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet but the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: When is an alcohol evaporator especially important?

options.text: In cold weather.
In hot weather.
In dry weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: In cold weather.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to stop ice from forming when it is cold.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes may squeak.
The brakes may not work.
The brakes may be slow to respond.
The brakes will be very sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may not work.
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too often can let air out faster than the compressor can replace it. If air pressure in the brake system gets too low, the brakes will stop working.

questions.question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:

options.text: Be swept clean.
Have rags in it.
Not be used to store cargo.
Have no cracks or damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have no cracks or damage.
questions.explanation: When you inspect an enclosed trailer, check the front for damage. Look for cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: When approaching a curve during the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following except:

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Slow down before entering the curve.
Keep your vehicle in its lane.
Use the brakes while going through the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes while going through the curve.
questions.explanation: When approaching a curve, check traffic in all directions. Slow down before entering the curve so you do not need to brake or shift while turning. Stay in your lane and keep checking traffic.

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being used by the brakes right now.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being used by the brakes right now.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure the brakes are using at that moment. It can help drivers know if their brakes are starting to fade.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 must have:

options.text: An extra set of brakes.
Voice-activated brakes.
Cruise control.
Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.correctAnswerText: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes made after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other vehicles with air brakes made after March 1, 1998 must also have ABS.

questions.question: What does a vehicle inspection report do?

options.text: Tells the company about problems that need fixing.
Makes sure the vehicle is checked regularly.
Makes drivers responsible for inspecting the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tells the company about problems that need fixing.
questions.explanation: Drivers may need to write a vehicle inspection report at the end of each day. The company must fix any safety problems listed in the report or state that no fixes are needed.

questions.question: If someone pulls in front of you and you cannot stop, you should:

options.text: Hit the other vehicle since it will be their fault.
Turn to avoid the other vehicle.
Put your vehicle in reverse.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn to avoid the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: If another vehicle pulls in front of you, brake if you have room to stop safely. If you do not have room to stop, turning to avoid the other vehicle may be safer.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes ahead, you should:

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop safely away from the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely away from the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash with an aggressive driver, stop a safe distance away. Wait for police and tell them about the aggressive behavior you saw.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle can safely fit under a bridge, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Swerve as you pass under the bridge.
Slow down.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: While driving downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake pedal.

options.text: 5 mph
10 mph
15 mph
20 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 5 mph
questions.explanation: While driving downhill, hold down the brake pedal until your vehicle reaches a speed 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake. Repeat this process.

questions.question: As temperatures rise and ice on roads begins to melt, what happens?

options.text: It is especially safe to drive.
The road becomes more slippery.
Traction increases.
It is easier to identify slippery spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road becomes more slippery.
questions.explanation: Melting ice is much more slippery than solid ice. Drive with extra caution on melting ice.

questions.question: When using road speed to decide when to shift gears, you should:

options.text: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
Watch other vehicles and try to keep pace.
Watch other trucks and shift when they shift.
Use the speed limit as a guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
questions.explanation: Read your vehicle's manual to learn which speeds work for each gear. Watch your speedometer and shift up when needed. This is one of two ways to know when to shift (the other is engine speed).

questions.question: When loading a trailer, it is important to:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
Not worry about how cargo weight is spread out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Weight on each axle should be balanced—not too much and not too little. Wrong weight distribution can affect steering, reduce wheel grip, or damage the axles.

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light comes on, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving normally.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.
Call local law enforcement.
Safely pull off the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely pull off the road and stop.
questions.explanation: If the air pressure warning light or buzzer comes on while driving, stop immediately and park safely. This warning means there is a problem with the air brake system that needs to be fixed.

questions.question: When entering traffic, a large vehicle usually needs:

options.text: Less space than a car.
About the same space as a car.
More space than a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: More space than a car.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more space to enter or cross traffic than cars. This is because they are bigger and need more distance to speed up.

questions.question: When checking under your vehicle for leaks, you should look for all of the following, except:

options.text: Fresh oil.
Coolant.
Grease.
Windshield wiper fluid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Windshield wiper fluid.
questions.explanation: Before driving, look under your vehicle for leaks of oil, coolant, grease, or fuel.

questions.question: To use controlled braking, you should:

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Press the brakes with about half strength.
Press the brakes until the wheels lock.
Pump the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. If you need to steer while braking, release the brakes, steer, then press the brakes again.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Cracked drums
Shoes with oil or grease on them
Shoes worn very thin
Pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: Check your brakes for cracked drums; shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them; and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn dangerously thin.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move into the left lane.
Speed up.
Increase the space in front of your vehicle.
Flash your lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space in front of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, give them more space in front of your vehicle. This makes it easier for them to pass you. Speeding up does not help because they will just tailgate you at the higher speed, creating more danger.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, what should a driver do?

options.text: Jump directly from the seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand on the vehicle.
Face the vehicle while exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face the vehicle while exiting.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during a driving test, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For buses, keep your hand on the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used to:

options.text: Make the air brakes work more effectively.
Temporarily release the spring brakes.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Temporarily release the spring brakes.
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they have been activated by low air pressure. Pressing the correct control releases the spring brakes for a short time, allowing you to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: What should you check when inspecting your tires before a trip?

options.text: Tire pressure.
Tire color.
Tire manufacturer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire pressure.
questions.explanation: When checking your tires before a trip, make sure the tire pressure is correct. It should not be too low or too high.

questions.question: When is a tank endorsement required?

options.text: Only when transporting gases.
Only when transporting liquids.
When transporting both liquids and gases.
It is optional when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: When transporting both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: You must have a tank endorsement to transport liquids or gases. This applies to both hazardous and non-hazardous substances, with some exceptions.

questions.question: When making a tight turn or maneuver, you should:

options.text: Not use your mirrors because they are distracting.
Use your mirrors, but not too often.
Check your mirrors frequently.
Only rely on your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors frequently.
questions.explanation: When making tight turns or maneuvers, check your mirrors often to stay aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the air brake system falls below 60 psi?

options.text: A warning light comes on.
Lights flash on the outside of the vehicle.
A message appears on the control panel.
The vehicle stops automatically.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light comes on.
questions.explanation: On vehicles with air brakes, a low air pressure warning light will come on if tank pressure falls below 60 psi. On large buses, the warning may activate at 80 to 85 psi.

questions.question: After an accident, which action is not recommended?

options.text: Try to move your vehicle to the side of the road.
Help the injured.
Drive away from the scene.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive away from the scene.
questions.explanation: After an accident, protect the area, call the authorities, help the injured, gather information, and report the accident. You can lose your license if you leave the scene of an accident.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: Stop cargo from moving during transport.
Prevent cargo from being loaded too high.
Prevent cargo from being unloaded too quickly.
Prevent cargo from being unloaded easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from moving during transport.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing are used to keep cargo from sliding during transport.

questions.question: What should you do when conducting a pre-drive inspection?

options.text: The inspection report is not important.
Only review the inspection report if passengers will be in the vehicle.
Review the previous inspection report, if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the previous inspection report, if one exists.
questions.explanation: The first step of a vehicle inspection is to review the last inspection report. Only sign the new report if any defects from the previous report have been fixed.
